note:
FEATURE / GPU RENDERING / BATCHED EXTRACTION + PUBLICATION: This ticket continues the architecture identified from the `gpu-v2` VoxelShowcase performance work. It is NOT blocked on `gpu-v2` promotion to master. At assignment start, fetch current `origin/master` and `origin/gpu-v2`, create or resume the assigned feature branch from current master as normal, then merge current `origin/gpu-v2` into that feature branch before implementation. Resolve only in-scope GPU/rendering conflicts; do not reimplement the GPU foundation from master or create a parallel renderer. Re-read the merged implementation and evidence before editing. The reviewed baseline already preserves CPU voxel world truth, persistent GPU brick mirroring, demand recovery, compact payload scatter, snapshotless admission, stale-result rejection, old-mesh retention, private extraction scratch, arena publication, and zero eligible CPU fallback for supported work.

OBSERVED BOTTLENECK: The current safe path serializes GPU surface work through one global extraction-stage ticket per frame. A normal non-empty chunk progresses through count dispatch -> CPU counter readback -> write dispatch -> CPU verification/readback -> copy dispatch -> publish. Count, write, retry, and copy compete for the same safety ticket. One stage per frame keeps ordinary walking frames much healthier but cannot fill visible demand fast enough; reviewed evidence still showed roughly 400-542 missing chunks. Increasing to two private-scratch stages restored large Metal stalls, showing that simply raising per-frame dispatch concurrency is not a valid fix. The remaining problem is therefore GPU publication throughput and synchronization architecture, not another CPU micro-optimization.

PRIMARY GOAL: Replace per-chunk CPU-controlled count/write/copy handshakes with a bounded batched GPU extraction/publication pipeline. CPU voxels remain authoritative for gameplay/world truth; the GPU should own derived rendering work from mirror lookup through sizing/allocation, meshing, publication metadata, indirect args, and draw-ready output. CPU may observe coarse completion/version/diagnostic state but must not synchronously steer every chunk stage or read back geometry counts as rendering truth.

REQUIRED DISCRIMINATOR / TELEMETRY: Before changing architecture, add bounded production telemetry that measures the throughput funnel per interval: requested -> mirror-ready -> count-ready -> written -> copied/published, plus queue age, completed chunks/sec, visible missing demand, stale rejection, retries, fallback, and bounded memory/in-flight counts. Use this to prove where visible-first demand outruns publication and to evaluate each architecture change. Do not diagnose progress only from screenshots or aggregate FPS.

BATCHED GPU PIPELINE: Implement the smallest reusable mechanism that lets multiple chunk requests progress without a CPU round-trip between every phase. The intended shape is descriptor batch -> GPU classify/count -> GPU prefix/sizing/allocation -> GPU mesh/write into unpublished storage -> GPU publication metadata/indirect args -> version-safe publish. Exact implementation may differ, but per-chunk synchronous counter readback must not remain the steady-state scheduling mechanism. Preserve bounded allocation, deterministic source-version ownership, stale-result rejection, unsupported-semantics fallback, and previous-ready geometry until replacement publication is valid.

RESOURCE ORDERING / RENDERGRAPH: Replace the crude global one-operation-per-frame safety barrier with explicit compute/copy/draw resource ordering where practical, preferably through Unity RenderGraph or an equivalent repository-owned dependency model. The important contract is explicit mirror-read, scratch/write, arena-copy/publication, indirect-args, and draw ordering. RenderGraph is not itself the performance goal; it is the mechanism that should make safe overlap/batching possible without live-arena hazards. Do not introduce unbounded command-buffer queues, hidden fences, synchronous waits, or a second rendering path.

VISIBILITY / BACKPRESSURE: Visible holes must outrank prefetch and low-value background work. Batch admission must be bounded by device/profile budgets and must expose deterministic backpressure rather than allowing queue growth. Presentation tiers may change capacity or batch size, never correctness. Avoid starvation of newly visible chunks, recovery work, retries, or publication completion. CPU/HLOD/far fallback behavior must remain semantically correct and must not become the normal path for supported near-ring work.

LIFECYCLE / FAILURE SAFETY: Add focused coverage for batch admission, scratch reuse, allocation failure, retry, stale source versions, cancellation, device/resource disposal, scene/domain reload, arena lease release, zero-geometry completion, unsupported semantics, and shutdown with in-flight work. A failed or stale batch must not leak buffers/leases, publish partial geometry, corrupt indirect args, or discard the previous valid mesh.

PERFORMANCE / BUILT-PLAYER VALIDATION: Validate in the actual built `VoxelShowcase` player, not only EditMode/PlayMode. Preserve the existing moving/stationary performance gates unless evidence justifies a stricter one: moving p95 <18 ms and p99 <25 ms; stationary p95 <8 ms. Run the 8-build traversal profile under the existing memory wrapper and then the full 150 s acceptance traversal. Record CPU frame timing, GPU/extraction throughput, missing-visible coverage, fallback, stale/retry counts, arena failures, GPU/CPU memory, and peak in-flight work. The architecture is not accepted merely because frame times improve while visible coverage falls behind.

VISUAL ACCEPTANCE: Exact built-player captures must show complete near/mid terrain during traversal with no broad rectangular ground holes, seams, frozen missing regions, or publication-induced popping. Inspect player-height and moving frames, not only the final converged survey frame. Rendering correctness and visual continuity are separate gates from throughput metrics.

ACCEPTANCE: (1) the merged `gpu-v2` CPU-authoritative world truth and reusable GPU mirror/extraction semantics remain authoritative; (2) production rendering no longer depends on a CPU readback/decision round-trip between every chunk count/write/publication phase; (3) resource ordering is explicit enough that multiple chunks can make useful progress safely without the current one-global-stage-per-frame bottleneck or Metal-style live-arena contention; (4) requested-to-published throughput and queue-age telemetry proves visible demand can be serviced without persistent accumulation; (5) supported near-ring work retains zero eligible CPU fallback and correct stale/version semantics; (6) allocation, scratch, arena, indirect-args, retry, cancellation, and disposal behavior are bounded and regression-tested; (7) the 8-build built-player traversal meets frame budgets while converging visible coverage instead of leaving hundreds of chunks missing; (8) the full 150 s built-player traversal meets moving/stationary gates, has no blocking waits/arena failures, and remains within existing memory/device budgets; and (9) full-resolution built-player evidence passes human visual review with no broad holes/seams or publication artifacts.

NON-GOALS: Moving gameplay/collision/replication/world truth to the GPU; changing voxel storage semantics; weakening performance or visual gates; hiding missing geometry with non-authoritative cover meshes; increasing concurrency without measured safe ordering; continuing unrelated CPU micro-optimization experiments already falsified by the GPU evidence; or creating a parallel renderer.

START RULE: This issue may be assigned immediately. The worker must fetch both current refs, start from current `origin/master`, merge current `origin/gpu-v2` into its own assigned feature branch, and perform all implementation/validation there. Do not wait for `gpu-v2` to reach master and do not merge `gpu-v2` directly to master as a prerequisite. After that merge, create and maintain the worker's `plan.md` and `tasks.md` and follow the normal SceneIssue exact-SHA validation and final-master merge workflow.
